title: nesting rules not transformed correctly when targeting older browsers
impact: Targets without :is() (Chrome < 88, Safari < 14, Firefox < 78), e.g. legacy Electron/WPE/embedded Chromium (reporters of #202 and #1159). Duplicates: #944 (closed by maintainer as dup of #202), #1159 (open, same request for a complex parent). Related umbrella: #312. 1 reaction here, 1 on #1159. The silent part (no warning) is what hurts: the whole rule is dropped by those browsers.
code: src/selector.rs: serialize_nesting (writes :is() at print time, so it never gets the :-webkit-any() fallback that hand-written :is() gets)
summary: With a multi-selector parent (or a complex parent with & not leftmost), nesting is lowered to `:is(...)` regardless of targets, and no warning is emitted when targets lack :is(). Per the nesting spec `&` has :is() semantics (matching and max specificity), so :is() is correct in general and a naive expansion is not. But some cases can be lowered exactly (e.g. `.foo, .bar { & .baz }` -> `.foo .baz, .bar .baz` when all parents have equal specificity), and the remaining cases deserve a warning, as esbuild does.
repro: 202-repro.mjs. `.foo, .bar { & .baz { padding: 0 } }` chrome 55 -> `:is(.foo,.bar) .baz{padding:0}`, warnings []. `.foo .bar { .baz & {} }` -> `.baz :is(.foo .bar){...}`, no warning. Controls: single compound parent -> `.foo .bar`; mixed-specificity parents keep :is(); hand-written `:is(.foo,.bar) .baz` does get a `:-webkit-any()` fallback.
evidence: repro.mjs local + 1.31.1-1.33.0: identical output, no warnings. equivalence.mjs (Chromium 153): `.foo, .bar { & .baz }` vs `.foo .baz, .bar .baz` EQUIVALENT (with competing .baz/.q .baz rules); `.foo, #bar { & .baz }` vs expanded NOT EQUIVALENT (padding 3px vs 2px for an element matching .foo with a `.q.r .baz` competitor), confirming the maintainer's specificity point. probe.mjs: `:-webkit-any(#a,.b)` has pseudo-class weight only (loses to `.x.b`), unlike `:is(#a,.b)`, so a :-webkit-any() fallback is exact only when every argument has specificity (0,1,0). Spec: css-nesting #nest-selector, 'The nesting selector intentionally uses the same specificity rules as the :is() pseudoclass' (quoted by the maintainer in the thread).

fix.approach: (1) Small: when a lowered nesting selector needs :is() and targets lack IsSelector, emit a warning naming the rule (the maintainer's own concern in 2022). (2) Medium: expand to a plain selector list when exact: all parent selectors have equal specificity, & occurs once, and either & is the leftmost compound or every parent is a single compound selector; cap the size (n^k with several &). Optionally route generated :is() through the existing :-webkit-any() fallback when every argument is a single (0,1,0) compound.

draftReply:
Still current on 1.33.0: `.foo, .bar { & .baz {} }` becomes `:is(.foo, .bar) .baz` even for Chrome 55, with no warning. As discussed above, `&` is defined with `:is()` semantics, so `:is()` is the correct output in general, and expanding it can change matching or specificity (e.g. `.foo, #bar { & .baz {} }`).

Some cases could be lowered exactly, though: when all parent selectors have the same specificity, `.foo .baz, .bar .baz` is equivalent. For the rest, a warning when the targets don't support `:is()` would at least make the problem visible. Whether to do either is up to the maintainer; #1159 and #944 ask for the same thing.

Workaround today: for old targets, write the expanded selectors by hand or avoid nesting under selector lists.
